name: Museo La Tertulia
funding: Private museum, ~2,000 works (2025); funded by Colegio Alemán de Cali as major patron, Bancolombia, Fundación Sura, Comfandi and Fundación Scarpetta Gnecco.
watch: Bancolombia (bank) and Sura (insurer) are named in the museum's own June 2025 statement.
records_note: Its web address redirects to a Linktree page of ticket links and a friends-program file; no reports, accounts, funder list or board are published.

name: Museo Larco
watch: Pre-Columbian collection. Led by president and CEO Andrés Álvarez Calderón Larco.
records_note: Larco publishes no annual reports, accounts or sponsors; its directory names only an executive president and a director, not a board.

name: Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno Carlos Mérida (MUNAM)
funding: State museum of the Ministerio de Cultura y Deportes, which spent over Q16M (about US$2M) on roof and museography works in 2023-25.
watch: Closed since Nov 2022, with no reopening date as of Oct 2025.
records_note: The museum has only a page on its ministry's site with no reports, funders or board; the ministry posts budget execution for the whole ministry.

name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
funding: Federal state museum. Its Friends association lists corporate members Banco Hipotecario, Bagó, Gador, Hospital Alemán, KPMG, Compañía Sudamericana de Dragados and Nicholson y Cano.
records_note: The museum's own site is blocked, but its Friends association lists corporate members and a board, undated; no accounts or reports were found.

name: Museo Nacional de Etnografía y Folklore (MUSEF)
funding: State museum (60 years in 2022) funded through the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, a public body under the central bank.
watch: Holds more than 33,000 cultural objects. Its director was pushed out in 2020 after a change of government and reinstated in 2021.
records_note: MUSEF has no records of its own; parent Fundación Cultural del BCB posts reports 2019 to 2025, statements 2018 to 2025 and its council.

name: Museo Nacional del Ecuador (MuNa)
funding: State national museum; the government has budgeted about US$100M for a new building, with a state-owned enterprise managing construction.
watch: The government overturned the jury's choice of design for the new building in July 2026.
records_note: The museum's site and its ministry's site both block automated access, so nothing could be checked.

name: Museo para la Identidad Nacional (MIN)
funding: Small foundation museum (930k visitors 2006-2019) run by the Fundación Hondureña para la Identidad Nacional; donors not published.
watch: The board was named in Nov 2022 to steer the museum through 'the greatest financial crisis' in its history. The sponsor block on its site is empty.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; nine unlabelled, undated logos show as pillar partners; the foundation board, appointed November 2022, is named in full.

name: Museo Popol Vuh
funding: Small university museum of Universidad Francisco Marroquín, supported by corporate room sponsorships; the last roster published is for 2019.
watch: Pre-Hispanic and colonial collection. The sponsors page (edited Dec 2025) still lists 2019 sponsors: Pepsi/CBC, Pollo Campero and CMI.
records_note: The museum has no records of its own; its parent university posts audited statements and annual reports, and its sponsor page shows three 2019 logos.

name: Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza
funding: Ministry of Culture operating subsidies, ticket sales, commercial retail, private patrons.
records_note: Activity reports run 2017 to 2024, audited accounts 2013 to 2025 are posted, the 2024 accounts name sponsors with amounts, and the Patronato is listed.

name: Museo Universitario del Chopo
watch: Sol Henaro has directed it since 2024. A Juan Gabriel show due 28 May 2026 was postponed with no reason given.
records_note: The Chopo's site names no sponsors; owner UNAM posts audited accounts for 2022 to 2025 and names its governing boards.

name: Museu de Arte Brasileira da FAAP
funding: Kept by the private university foundation FAAP, created in 1947 from the Penteado estate. The 2026 MAM show runs on Lei Rouanet and São Paulo's PROMAC; no company is named.
records_note: The museum's page and its parent foundation FAAP's legal page post no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board.

name: Museu de Arte Moderna da Bahia
watch: The state tendered the museum's restaurant and pier to private operators in 2024.
records_note: A Bahia state museum run through the cultural institute IPAC; its own site refused connection and IPAC's site posts no museum accounts.
